header.title: Mahabharat Episode 3: Curses or Blessings?
header.description: The story of a friendship turned bitter between Devyani and Princess Sharmishtha, King Yayati's secret affair, and the exchange of youth that shaped the Kuru dynasty.

intro.title: The Fine Line Between Curses and Boons
leads: Throughout the story of the Mahabharat, human destinies are constantly shaped by powerful curses and boons.
Yet, life has a surprising way of mixing things up—what seems like a terrible curse often turns into a blessing, and a grand boon can easily lead to ruin.
This episode reveals how a simple argument between two young friends at a riverbank became the very root of the great Yadava and Kuru dynasties.

storyElements.html: Devyani (daughter of the sage Shukracharya) and Sharmishtha (daughter of the Asura King Vrishaparva) were close friends.
Devyani belonged to the priest class (Brahmin), which was held in high social regard, while Sharmishtha was a royal princess.
One day, the two young women went to the river together to bathe and left their clothes and jewelry in separate piles on the bank.
While they were playing in the water, a strong wind blew and mixed up their clothes.
Hurrying out of the river to get dressed, Princess Sharmishtha accidentally put on some of Devyani's clothes.

bubble.text: How can you wear the clothes of your father’s guru’s daughter? How does that feel, and how is it appropriate?

storyElements.html: Sharmishtha realized her mistake, but being a proud princess, she flew into a furious rage at being lectured.

bubble.text: Your father is a beggar! He bows down before my father and lives off what my father gives him. You better learn your place!

storyElements.html: In anger, Sharmishtha pushed Devyani into a dry pit and walked away, leaving her trapped.
After being rescued, Devyani ran home crying to her father, Shukracharya, demanding that the princess be punished.
Angered by the insult to his daughter, Shukracharya threatened to abandon the Asura kingdom.
King Vrishaparva had no choice but to yield, as the kingdom relied entirely on Shukracharya's Sanjeevini mantra to survive wars.
As punishment, Princess Sharmishtha was forced to become Devyani’s personal maid servant.
Later, when Devyani married King Yayati (son of Nahusha), she insisted that Sharmishtha accompany her to her new royal home as her maid.
King Yayati and Devyani lived together and had a son named Yadu. The famous Yadava lineage descends from him.
Even though Sharmishtha served as a maid, she maintained her royal grace and beauty.
Inevitably, King Yayati fell secretly in love with Sharmishtha.
They had a secret romance and produced a child named Puru, who would become a key ancestor of the Kuru dynasty.

storyElements.text: The Curse of Sudden Old Age

storyElements.html: Eventually, Shukracharya discovered that King Yayati had betrayed Devyani by secretly having a child with her maid.

bubble.text: You have betrayed my daughter! May you instantly lose your youth and become an old man!

storyElements.html: Instantly, King Yayati was transformed into a frail, old man.
Unable to accept losing his youth so suddenly, Yayati searched for a way to enjoy life once more.
King Yayati turned to his eldest son, Yadu, asking him for a favor.

bubble.text: Give me your youth so I can enjoy life for a few more years, and I will give it back to you later.
No way! First you cheated my mother, and now you want to take my youth!

storyElements.html: Furious at Yadu's refusal, Yayati cursed his eldest son.

bubble.text: May you and your descendants never inherit the throne!

storyElements.html: Then Yayati asked his younger son, Puru (born to Sharmishtha).

bubble.text: Father, please take my youth and enjoy it. My youth means nothing to me compared to your happiness.

storyElements.html: Puru willingly gave up his youth and took on his father's old age.
Yayati lived as a young man for many years until he was finally satisfied. He then returned youth to Puru and crowned him as the new king.
Though Puru was the younger son of a maid servant, his selfless devotion granted him the throne, establishing the royal lineage of the Kurus...
